claim: Tailwind 4 auto-detects classes starting from the current working directory, skips .gitignore'd files, node_modules, binary files, CSS files and lock files; @source paths are resolved relative to the CSS file, and source(none) disables auto-detection entirely.
quote: Tailwind uses the current working directory as its starting point when scanning for class names... it ignores: Files listed in your .gitignore file... Files in the node_modules directory... @source "../node_modules/@acmecorp/ui-lib";

claim: Nx's official React guide states Tailwind v4 auto-detection with the Vite plugin only scans the app directory, so libs must be added explicitly with @source directives such as @source "../../../libs/ui".

Nx blog: with @tailwindcss/vite in an npm/pnpm workspace, styles defined in workspace packages are omitted from the bundle unless @source directives point at each package, producing missing styles and broken layouts.
quote: Tailwind only scans the main app by default. This means styles defined in your packages won't be included in the final bundle, leading to missing styles and broken layouts.

claim: tailwindlabs/tailwindcss issue #13136 (opened 7 Mar 2024, now closed) reported that v4 automatic content detection in monorepos only finds the direct package and that relative base paths did not work, prompting the explicit @source escape hatch.
quote: v4: Automatic content detection in monorepos only finds direct package

claim: Aug 2025 discussion: a React+TS+Vite monorepo saw zero Tailwind utilities applied from a shared component library; Tailwind collaborator wongjn traced it to the library's package.json CSS exports and a missing CSS import in the consumer app, not just @source.
quote: When rendering a component from the library in the app, no Tailwind utilities apply

claim: Tailwind 4.1.5 monorepo discussion: utilities generated in dev but missing in production build; root causes were @source paths pointing at non-existent directories and the UI package not exporting its theme CSS via package.json exports.
quote: The CSS output contains only theme variables and base styles, missing utility classes like .bg-red-500 and .text-white

claim: Nx + Angular Tailwind 4 upgrade thread (Jan-Apr 2025): 'Cannot apply unknown utility class: bg-white' errors, fixed by .postcssrc.json with @tailwindcss/postcss, adding @reference to component stylesheets using @apply, and switching from @nx/angular:webpack-browser to browser-esbuild.
quote: Cannot apply unknown utility class: bg-white [plugin angular-sass]

claim: Nx discussion #29810 (opened 30 Jan 2025): users waited months for native Tailwind v4 support while Nx 21 still generated Tailwind 3.x configs; in Feb 2026 maintainer @juristr announced Nx will disable its native Tailwind integration and point users at the official Tailwind guides plus a community sync generator.
quote: Nx would disable the native Tailwind integration instead. The recommendation was adopting official Tailwind guides with community-provided solutions including: A sync generator for monorepo environments

claim: Nx maintains a dedicated blog guide for wiring Tailwind v4 into an Nx workspace, reflecting that Tailwind 4 setup in Nx is now a documented manual process rather than an Nx executor feature.
quote: Configure Tailwind v4 with Angular in an Nx Monorepo

claim: @juristr/nx-tailwind-sync is an Nx sync generator that walks the Nx project graph and auto-writes @source directives for all transitive dependencies into the app's CSS; latest version 0.0.9 published 2026-02-10, sole maintainer juristr (Nx core team).
quote: Nx sync generator that auto-manages `@source` directives in CSS files for Tailwind v4 monorepos.

claim: shadcn/ui's manual installation now lists tw-animate-css (not tailwindcss-animate) as the required animation dependency.
quote: pnpm add shadcn class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react tw-animate-css

claim: tw-animate-css is a solo-maintained MIT project by Wombosvideo (Luca Bosin): 781 stars, 13 forks, 18 open issues, created 2025-01-28, last push 2026-02-28; 90 of ~99 commits are the owner's and a breaking v2.0.0 is still pending.
quote: This package is a replacement for `tailwindcss-animate`. ... The upcoming release v2.0.0 will include breaking changes. A migration script and a guide will be provided to help you transition smoothly.

claim: tailwindcss-animate (jamiebuilds) has 3,030 stars but its repo was last pushed 2024-07-28 and its last npm release 1.0.7 shipped 2023-08-28 - it is a Tailwind v3 JS plugin, unmaintained rather than formally npm-deprecated.
quote: tailwindcss-animate - A Tailwind CSS plugin for creating beautiful animations.

claim: npm registry: tw-animate-css latest is 1.4.0 published 2025-09-24 (only a canary 1.3.0-canary.35 since, 2026-02-28); single maintainer wombosvideo; ~35.5M downloads in the week of 2026-07-05, versus ~21.6M for the legacy tailwindcss-animate.

claim: Tailwind discussion #18270 (10 Jun 2025) quotes the official floor verbatim: Tailwind CSS v4.0 targets Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+ and Firefox 128+, with users requesting wider browser support.
quote: Tailwind CSS v4.0 is designed for Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+, and Firefox 128+.

claim: Firefox 128 (released 9 July 2024) is the first Firefox to ship the CSS @property at-rule and CSS.registerProperty() by default - which is exactly why Tailwind 4's floor is Firefox 128.
quote: The CSSPropertyRule interface is now supported by default and represents a CSS @property at-rule... The registerProperty() method is now supported by default.

claim: color-mix() reached Baseline 'widely available' in May 2023 (Chrome 111 / Safari 16.2 / Firefox 113), which is the origin of Tailwind 4's Chrome 111 floor.
quote: Baseline: Widely available - Available across browsers since May 2023

claim: Chrome 111 (March 2023) is the release that shipped color-mix().
quote: When using color-mix(), which enables mixing a percentage of one color into another, you can view the final color output in the Computed pane.

claim: @property became Baseline 'newly available' in July 2024, i.e. it is the newest of Tailwind 4's three hard requirements (@property, color-mix(), cascade layers) and therefore sets the browser floor.
quote: Baseline 2024 - Newly available - Since July 2024, this feature works across the latest devices and browser versions.

claim: Juri Strumpflohner (Nx core team) maintains a reference repo demonstrating Tailwind 4 + Vite across npm workspaces with explicit @source directives.
quote: tailwind4-vite-npm-workspaces
